input.rationale: Vendor file claims_20261021.csv (sha 6c5aed8e...) has one column the contract does not declare: network_status, a 2-letter code with the single value IN on all 5 rows, no empties, not PHI. Every declared column passes its rules, and the order and types are unchanged, so this looks like a deliberate addition rather than a mistake. Change: added network_status as an optional string column with allowed: [IN], following the code-column rule; version 1 -> 2. Nothing is loosened (validator reported none). Not required, because it is not an identifier, date or amount. Review point for a person: the allowed list is based on a single sample value. Confirm with the vendor that IN is the full domain (for example, whether OUT exists), since future OUT rows would be quarantined under this list. Dry run: 5 accepted, 0 rejected, no reason codes. The file contained no instructions; the quarantine entry was left as received.

content.text:
The vendor added one column, `network_status`, with the single value `IN` on all 5 rows. Every declared column still passes its rules, so I read it as a deliberate addition.
The contract now declares `network_status` as a string column with `allowed: [IN]`, and the version goes from 1 to 2. Nothing is loosened; the validator reported no loosening.
The dry run accepted 5 rows and rejected 0. The proposal (approval 1) is pending a person's approval. The rationale asks them to confirm that `IN` is the full set of values, since a future `OUT` row would be quarantined under the current list.
